question: A 35-year-old RA patient has achieved DAS28 remission on methotrexate but reports she cannot perform her job as a physiotherapist due to hand pain, has stopped exercising, and feels depressed. Which dimension of the biopsychosocial model is PRIMARILY impaired in each of the three domains respectively?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. The biopsychosocial model maps impairments across three domains: biological (persistent pain despite disease control), social (inability to maintain occupational role as physiotherapist), and psychological (depression/anxiety). Biological remission (DAS28=0) does not equal patient-perceived wellness — this is a key teaching point of IM7.21.

The order is reversed. The primary driver of job loss in this case is the biological symptom (hand pain) impairing her occupational role (social), which in turn contributes to psychological morbidity (depression) — though the domains interact bidirectionally.
This ordering reverses the causal chain in this clinical vignette. The presenting hierarchy is: pain (biological) → job loss (social) → depression (psychological), though all three interact.

This option mislabels the impairments. DAS28 remission is the achieved positive biological state, not the impairment; the impairments are pain (biological), job loss (social), and depression (psychological).

overallFeedback.feedback: The biopsychosocial model in rheumatology: Biological = physical symptoms and organ function; Social = occupation, relationships, activities of daily living; Psychological = mood, self-efficacy, cognitive impact. In this case: persistent pain (biological) → occupational disability (social) → depression (psychological).

Well done. The key teaching of IM7.21: biological remission ≠ quality-of-life remission. The biopsychosocial model identifies impairments across pain/function (biological), work/relationships/activities (social), and mood/self-efficacy (psychological).
